chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man comes and says, 'Buy this garment and I will profit you so-and-so.' He said: 'Is it not that if he wishes, he leaves it, and if he wishes, he takes it?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'There is no harm with it. It is the speech that makes permissible and the speech that makes forbidden.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a seller to offer a specific profit margin to encourage a buyer to purchase a good?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the commercial practice of offering a specific profit margin to incentivize a sale, emphasizing that such proposals are non-binding until accepted. The Imam highlights the jurisprudential principle that 'speech alone does not create obligation nor prohibition,' distinguishing between mere negotiation and the formalization of a contract. This underscores the flexibility in Shia commercial law where verbal offers serve as invitations rather than binding commitments, preserving the buyer's autonomy.
